I am 58 years old and have farmed my land in Quzhou for over 35 years. I finished primary school and that was enough to learn what I need. My family has about 10 mu of good flat land on the North China Plain. I know this soil like the back of my hand.

This year, I will do what has always worked for my family. I will plant **8 mu of winter wheat** and follow it with **summer maize on the same 8 mu** after the wheat comes off in early June. That is our backbone — we eat the wheat as flour, sell the surplus, and the maize goes to feed and cash. I will also keep **2 mu of cotton** on the side. My wife insists on it because cotton brings good money, though at my age all that bending and spraying is getting hard on my back. I have cut the cotton down from 3 mu last year.

For the wheat, I will use **improved seeds** — probably Lüyuan 502, same as last year. Before planting, I will do **rotary tillage** to break up the stubble and smooth the field. I will apply about **7 kg of nitrogen per mu** (mostly urea) and not bother with phosphorus or potassium — our soil here on the plain does not need it. The wheat needs **4 irrigations**: green-up water, jointing water, heading water, and grain-filling water. I will spray pesticides **4 times** to keep aphids, weeds, and rust under control. If the weather cooperates like last year, I expect about **1000 kg per mu**.

After I harvest the wheat in June, there is no time to waste. I will plant **hybrid maize** — Dénghǎi 605 or something similar from the seed shop. I will **not till** the soil; I will plant directly into the wheat stubble because the summer season is short and every day matters. The maize needs **3 irrigations** and about **5 kg of nitrogen per mu**. I will spray **4 times** for insects and weeds. Hybrid maize should give me around **1100 kg per mu**.

For the cotton, I will use **improved seed** and do **rotary tillage** in April. Cotton is a money crop but it is thirsty for labor. I will irrigate **2 times** and put down about **9 kg of nitrogen per mu**. The worst part is the spraying — cotton bollworm is relentless here, so I will spray pesticides **17 times** through the season. If I am lucky, the 2 mu will give me **500 kg per mu** of seed cotton.

I do not try fancy new crops. I am too old to gamble with my family's food. Wheat and maize are safe because the government guarantees the wheat price, and the seed dealer gives me credit for hybrid maize seed. Cotton is hard work, but the cash helps when my grandson needs school fees.
